name: Evening hot shower / bath
lead: The evening hot shower or bath is a pre-bed routine that proponents say promotes sleep onset by relaxing the body and, as it cools afterward, lowering core temperature.

This claim is circulated in sleep and looksmaxxing communities; Wikipedia articles on sleep onset and hot tubs, the pages reviewed for this entry, do not cover it, and the hot tub article notes only that sitting in water above normal body temperature can cause drowsiness, presented as a drowning risk.[1]
Source material for this entry is thin.

paras: Practitioners take a warm or hot shower or bath in the evening before bed. Proponents attribute faster sleep onset to the temperature change afterward.
The hot tub article notes that sitting in water above normal body temperatures can cause drowsiness, which is a drowning risk in that setting.[1]
No clinical studies were covered in the sources reviewed for this article.

lore.intro: A warm evening shower is discussed as a simple sleep aid.

claims.claim: A hot shower or bath before bed helps you fall asleep faster
claims.believers: Proponents report feeling drowsy after bathing and falling asleep sooner.
claims.experts: Sources reviewed here do not examine this claim.

card.summary: A warm shower or bath before bed for faster sleep onset; thinly sourced here.
card.note: Very hot water can cause drowsiness or dizziness.

quick.overview:
The practice is a warm shower or bath in the evening to ease into sleep.

Sources reviewed for this wiki do not test the claim.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say the body cools after the bath, signaling sleep.
quick.risks: Very hot water can cause drowsiness; the hot tub article treats that as a drowning risk.[1]
